prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"I need something to drink at a barbecue that tastes like spices, but nothing too heavy."

List A:
Wine 1: Syrah, US, $34. Tasting note: "A beautiful Syrah, softly tannic, dry and full bodied. High alcohol gives some jalapeño pepper heat to the blackberries, licorice, bacon, dark chocolate and sandalwood flavors, but nothing that richly sauced barbecue can't handle. Drink up."
Wine 2: Zinfandel, US, $24. Tasting note: "Barbecue is your best bet with this rustic Zin. It's lusty in jammy blackberry, mulberry and vanilla spice flavors that finish with a definite sugariness."
Wine 3: Zinfandel, US, $30. Tasting note: "Heavy in alcohol and overripe, but entirely dry, and the black currant, chocolate and pepper flavors will play well against richly sauced barbecue."
Wine 4: Red Blend, US, $17. Tasting note: "There's a robust heartiness to this Rhône-style blend that makes it perfect for drinking on cold nights with spicy barbecue or stew. Mainly Syrah and Petite Sirah, it's rich in blackberry, bacon and black pepper flavors. Bone dry and moderate in alcohol, it represents great quality for the price, and it should be relatively easy to find, with nearly 12,000 cases produced."
Wine 5: Shiraz, Australia, $18. Tasting note: "Roasted meat, floral notes, peppery spice...sounds rather nice. Add in silky tannins, hints of coffee and blueberry and a long finish, and you have a pretty wine at a realistic price. Drink now-2014."

List B:
Wine 1: Zinfandel, US, $21. Tasting note: "Put some meat on the grill, slather it with barbecue sauce, and enjoy with this spicy Zin. Medium-bodied, it doesn't overwhelm the food but complements it, with dry, classically varietal flavors of wild berries, brambly herbs, white pepper and sandalwood."
Wine 2: Zinfandel, US, $22. Tasting note: "This is ripe and spicy, with plenty of blackberry and blueberry flavors. Although it's a little lighter on the palate than expected, it's fine for barbecue."
Wine 3: Zinfandel, US, $24. Tasting note: "Here's an exuberant, country-style Zin that's easy to drink with barbecue. It's enormously fruity in blackberries, currants, mulberries and cinnamon-spicy mocha, with firm tannins that need rich meats to unlock. Drink soon."
Wine 4: Zinfandel, US, $18. Tasting note: "This Zin tastes of smoke, oak and grilled meats, but has an odd acidity to it. It would be good paired with something off the barbecue."
Wine 5: Carmenère, Chile, $9. Tasting note: "This wine has such nice hickory, dried-spice and red-berry notes, it'd be a shame to drink it anywhere but outside on your deck, with some slow-cooked baby back ribs. Medium-weight, with some chalky tannins, it finishes with more of the same flavors, plus some char and green herb. Fire up the grill. Best Buy."
